summary: Yellowstone lookout about two miles east of West Yellowstone; listed gone by FFLA and firelookout.com. A private page dates it to 1935 and says footings remain visible on recent imagery.

facts.status_note: Listed as gone by firelookout.com and the FFLA; a privately run Google Sites page says its concrete footings are visible on recent Google Maps imagery

access.note: Inside Yellowstone National Park; the road is abandoned and the Google Sites page describes no road or trail to the site now

visit.trail_note: Road abandoned; essentially no road or trail to the site now, per the Google Sites page

events.note: Date given only by a privately run Google Sites page; no other page read gives a build date

evidence.supports: Lookout site is inside Yellowstone National Park
Site is about two miles east of West Yellowstone
firelookout.com calls the structure a tower
FFLA lists the structure as a platform, and gone
Google Sites page says the tower was built in 1935
Tower was marked on older topographic maps but not on newer ones
evidence.quote: marked on older topo maps but doesn't show on the more recent maps

evidence.supports: Lookout burned at some point, date not given
evidence.quote: The lookout burned down at some point.

evidence.supports: Concrete footings visible on recent Google Maps imagery
evidence.quote: The tower is gone, but the concrete footings are visible on the latest Google Maps imagery

evidence.supports: Road to the lookout has long been abandoned
evidence.quote: The road to the lookout has long been abandoned

evidence.supports: Essentially no road or trail to the site now
evidence.quote: there's essentially no road or trail there now

corrections.why: firelookout.com and the Google Sites page both describe a tower; the FFLA list says platform. The sources disagree, so the editor should decide.

notes_for_editor: Gone status is confirmed by two sources. The 1935 build date comes from one privately run Google Sites page. A Reddit thread found in search, which was not read in full, reportedly dates it to 1934, so the date is uncertain. Lead, not used: an NPS fire-lookout rephotography PDF (https://www.nps.gov/yell/learn/historyculture/upload/MSC049_FireRephoto_Update.pdf) has an index entry 'West Yellowstone Panoramic Photos, 1936'; the index does not say which lookout those photos show. Kind conflict is listed under corrections.
